title: Gap Filling, Editing & Transformation
description: Master the three core CBSE grammar question types for Grade 10: gap filling, editing (one error per line) and sentence transformation/rewriting — bilingual notes, practice and tests.

topics.title: Gap Filling & Editing
topics.concept:
Gap filling usually tests verbs (tense/form), articles, prepositions, conjunctions, determiners and modals. Use the words on both sides of the blank as clues, and keep the passage consistent.

Editing (one error per line): the standard CBSE format gives a passage where each line has exactly one mistake. You write the incorrect word and the correct word, like this:

IncorrectCorrect
gogoes
aan

Omission tasks mark a missing word with a caret; you supply the missing word and the words on either side.

examples.problem: Gap fill: She is good ___ painting and has ___ natural talent.
Edit (write incorrect → correct): He don't likes coffee.
examples.solution: don't → doesn't (and likes → like): 'He doesn't like coffee.'

recap: Gap filling tests verbs, articles, prepositions, determiners, modals
Editing = one error per line; write incorrect + correct word
Omission = supply the missing word with its neighbours

topics.title: Transformation / Rewriting (CBSE Format)
topics.concept:
Transformation asks you to rewrite a sentence as directed, keeping the meaning. Common directions:

  • Combine two sentences: He was tired. He kept working. → Though he was tired, he kept working.
  • Change the voice: She wrote a letter. → A letter was written by her.
  • Change the narration: He said, "I am busy." → He said that he was busy.
  • Begin with a given word: 'Rewrite beginning with "No sooner…"' or 'Begin with "Hardly…"'.
  • Rewrite using a given word (e.g. 'too', 'so', 'unless').

Always read the instruction carefully — the marks are for following the exact direction while preserving the meaning.

examples.problem: Rewrite using 'too…to': He is so weak that he cannot walk.
Begin with 'No sooner': As soon as he arrived, it started to rain.
examples.solution: No sooner had he arrived than it started to rain.

recap: Directions: combine, change voice, change narration, begin with…, use a word
Keep the meaning; follow the exact instruction

questions.q: Edit: 'She have a new phone.'
Gap fill: 'It is ___ useful tool.'
Edit: 'They was happy.'
Gap fill: 'He is good ___ cricket.'
Transform (so…that): 'It is too hot to drink.'
options: It is so hot that it cannot be drunk.
It is so hot to drink.
It is too hot that it cannot be drunk.
It is very hot to drink.

questions.q: Edit: 'I has finished.'
Voice: 'They are building a house.'
Narration: 'She said, "I am tired."'
options: She said that she was tired.
She said that I was tired.

questions.q: Omission — supply the word: 'She is one ___ the best.'
Edit: 'He don't care.'
Begin with 'Hardly': 'As soon as I entered, the lights went off.'
options: Hardly I entered when the lights went off.
Hardly had I entered when the lights went off.
Hardly did I entered than the lights went off.
Hardly I had entered the lights went off.

questions.q: Gap fill: 'You ___ wear a seatbelt.' (rule)
Edit the line (give both corrections): 'Neither the teacher nor the students was inform.'
questions.explanation: Agreement with nearer plural 'students' → 'were'; and 'informed' (passive participle).

questions.q: Transform, beginning with 'Scarcely': 'The moment the train started, it began to rain.'
options: Scarcely the train started when it began to rain.
Scarcely had the train started when it began to rain.
Scarcely did the train start than it began to rain.
Scarcely the train had started than it began to rain.

questions.q: Change the voice: 'People believe that he is innocent.'
options: It is believed that he is innocent.

questions.q: Gap fill (formal): 'Hardly ___ I reached the door when it slammed shut.'
Edit: 'The reason of his failure is because he was careless.'
Transform using 'in spite of': 'Though he was poor, he was happy.'
options: In spite of being poor, he was happy.
In spite of he was poor, he was happy.
In spite poor, he was happy.
In spite of poverty he happy was.
questions.explanation: 'In spite of + noun/gerund': 'In spite of being poor …'.

questions.q: Combine into a complex sentence: 'He worked hard. He wanted to succeed.'
options: He worked hard so that he could succeed.
He worked hard and wanted to succeed.
He worked hard, he wanted to succeed.
questions.explanation: Purpose clause: 'so that he could succeed'.

questions.q: Narration: 'He said to me, "Do not touch my things."'
options: He told me not to touch his things.
He said me to not touch his things.
He told that not to touch his things.
He asked me to touch his things.
questions.explanation: Negative command → 'told me not to + verb'.

outcomes: Solve gap-filling items (verbs, articles, prepositions, modals)
Do editing tasks: one error per line, with corrections
Transform sentences as directed (voice, narration, 'begin with…')
Apply the standard CBSE answer format

intro.en: Three question types appear in every CBSE grammar section: gap filling, editing, and transformation/rewriting. They are the highest-scoring, most predictable marks in the paper — if you know the format. This chapter drills all three so you answer them fast and correctly under time pressure.
intro.hi: हर CBSE grammar खंड में तीन प्रकार के प्रश्न आते हैं: gap filling, editing, और transformation/rewriting। यदि format आता है तो ये पेपर के सबसे अधिक अंक देने वाले, सबसे पूर्वानुमेय प्रश्न हैं। यह अध्याय तीनों का अभ्यास कराता है ताकि आप समय-दबाव में तेज़ी और शुद्धता से उत्तर दें।

real_life.situation:
A typical editing line and its answer format:

Line: Many student fails because they not revise.

Answer: student → students; not → do not (or 'don't')
real_life.why: Editing rewards precision in a fixed format — write the wrong word and the correction. Knowing that format, and scanning for one error per line, turns these into guaranteed marks.

rule_box.html:
TypeWhat to do
Gap fillingsupply the right word (verb/article/prep/modal)
Editingone error per line → write incorrect + correct
Omissiona word is missing → supply it with the words around it
Transformationrewrite as directed, keeping the meaning
rule_box.formula: Read the instruction → identify the grammar point → answer in the exact format
rule_box.example: Edit: 'He go to school' → go → goes.

quick_test.q: In CBSE editing, for each line you write:
options: the incorrect and the correct word
quick_test.explanation: The standard format requires the incorrect word and its correction.

common_mistakes.wrong: He is too weak that he cannot walk.
common_mistakes.right: He is so weak that he cannot walk.

common_mistakes.wrong: No sooner he arrived than it rained.
common_mistakes.right: No sooner had he arrived than it rained.

fill_l2.instructions: Edit — write the correction for the underlined error.

items.q: He is more taller than me. (more taller)
I am living here since 2015. (am living)

error_detection.sentence: She is the most cleverest girl.
Each of the boys have a bag.
error_detection.correct: Each of the boys has a bag.

sentence_correction.wrong: Rewrite using 'so…that': He is too tired to walk.
sentence_correction.correct: He is so tired that he cannot walk.

sentence_correction.wrong: Change the voice: She is writing a letter.
sentence_correction.correct: A letter is being written by her.

sentence_correction.wrong: Change the narration: He said, 'I will come.'
sentence_correction.correct: He said that he would come.

rearrangement.jumbled: to / weak / he / walk / is / too
rearrangement.answer: He is too weak to walk.

rearrangement.jumbled: was / by / the / letter / her / written
rearrangement.answer: The letter was written by her.

rearrangement.jumbled: that / busy / said / he / he / was
rearrangement.answer: He said that he was busy.

answers: Gap filling → supply the right word

reading.passage:
Editing task (one error per line, with corrections shown):

L1: Every morning my brother go for a walk. (go → goes)
L2: He believe that exercise keep him fit. (believe → believes)
L3: Yesterday he buyed new running shoes. (buyed → bought)
L4: He is more fitter than all his friends. (more fitter → fitter)

questions.q: What grammar point does Line 1 test?
What kind of error is 'buyed'?
questions.answer: A word-form error — the past of 'buy' is irregular: 'bought'.

questions.q: Why is 'more fitter' wrong?
questions.answer: It is a double comparative; 'fitter' alone is correct.

speaking: He goes to school by bus every day.
She has finished all her assignments.
We discussed the plan in detail.
No sooner had he left than it rained.
A new bridge has been built over the river.

writing.prompt: Write five short lines, each with one deliberate grammar error, then write the corrections beside them — like a CBSE editing exercise.
writing.example: Line: She don't like tea. (don't → doesn't)

micro_quiz.q: Transform (so…that): 'He is too short to reach.'
options: He is so short to reach.
He is so short that he cannot reach.
He is too short that he cannot reach.
He is very short to reach.

micro_quiz.q: Begin with 'No sooner': 'As soon as I slept, the phone rang.'
options: No sooner I slept than the phone rang.
No sooner had I slept than the phone rang.
No sooner did I slept than the phone rang.
No sooner I had slept the phone rang.

challenge.q: Transform using 'unless': 'If you do not hurry, you will miss the bus.'
options: Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus.
Unless you do not hurry, you will miss the bus.
Until you hurry, you will miss the bus.
If you hurry, you will miss the bus.

challenge.q: Change the voice: 'Someone has stolen my bike.'
options: My bike was stolen by someone.
challenge.explanation: Present perfect passive = has been + V3 (agent dropped).

challenge.q: Edit two errors: 'The childrens was playing in the park.'
